| extend ResponderRaw = coalesce(tostring(Owner.assignedTo), tostring(Owner.userPrincipalName))
| where isnotempty(ResponderRaw) and ResponderRaw !in~ ("Unassigned")
| extend Responder = iff(ResponderRaw contains "@", tostring(split(ResponderRaw, "@")[0]), ResponderRaw)
| summarize ClosedIncidents = dcount(IncidentNumber) by Month, Responder, Title
| order by Month asc, Responder asc, ClosedIncidents desc

name: Single Responder Monthly Trend
desc: Tracks a specific responder's monthly closed incident count over a year. Useful for individual performance tracking and 1:1 review preparation.
kql:
// NOTE: Replace accountid with the responder's account name and adjust dates
let start = datetime(2025-01-01);
let end   = datetime(2026-01-01);
let responder = "accountid";
SecurityIncident
| where Status == "Closed"
| where isnotempty(CreatedTime) and isnotempty(ClosedTime)
| where ClosedTime >= start and ClosedTime < end
| extend Month = format_datetime(ClosedTime, "yyyy-MM")
| extend ResponderRaw = coalesce(tostring(Owner.assignedTo), tostring(Owner.userPrincipalName))
| where isnotempty(ResponderRaw) and ResponderRaw !in~ ("Unassigned")
| extend Responder = iff(ResponderRaw contains "@", tostring(split(ResponderRaw, "@")[0]), ResponderRaw)
| where Responder =~ responder
| summarize ClosedCount = count() by Month
| order by Month asc

name: Top 10 Closed Incident Types
desc: Shows the top 10 most frequently closed incident types (by title/detection rule name). Helps identify which detections generate the most work and may be candidates for automation or tuning.

name: Yearly Responder MTTR Performance
desc: Annual MTTR performance per responder with closed count, average/P50/P90 resolution times. Designed for year-end SOC performance reviews and identifying training needs.
kql:
// NOTE: Adjust start and end dates to your reporting period
let monthStart = datetime(2025-01-01);
let monthEnd   = datetime(2026-01-01);
SecurityIncident
| where Status == "Closed"
| where isnotempty(CreatedTime) and isnotempty(ClosedTime)
| where ClosedTime >= monthStart and ClosedTime < monthEnd
| extend ResponderRaw = coalesce(tostring(Owner.assignedTo), tostring(Owner.userPrincipalName))
| where isnotempty(ResponderRaw) and ResponderRaw !in~ ("Unassigned")
| extend Responder = iff(ResponderRaw contains "@", tostring(split(ResponderRaw, "@")[0]), ResponderRaw)
| extend ResolveMinutes = (ClosedTime - CreatedTime) / 1m
| summarize
    ClosedCount = count(),
    MTTR_Min = avg(ResolveMinutes),
    P50_Min  = percentile(ResolveMinutes, 50),
    P90_Min  = percentile(ResolveMinutes, 90)
  by Responder
| order by ClosedCount desc

name: OAuth Consent and App Registration Summary
desc: Summarizes all OAuth consent grants, app role assignments, permission grants, new app registrations and service principal additions over 7 days. Shows which apps received consent, how many times and by whom. Broader than illicit consent detection. Covers all consent activity for governance review.
kql:
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has_any ("Consent to application", "Add app role assignment", "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant", "Add application", "Add service principal")
| extend InitiatedBy = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
| extend TargetApp = tostring(TargetResources[0].displayName)
| extend TargetAppId = tostring(TargetResources[0].id)
| summarize 
    ConsentCount = count(),
    LastConsent = max(TimeGenerated),
    Users = make_set(InitiatedBy, 10)
    by OperationName, TargetApp, TargetAppId
| order by ConsentCount desc

name: Active Account Password Age Report
desc: Comprehensive password age report for all active (non-disabled) accounts combining MDI IdentityAccountInfo and IdentityInfo tables. Shows days/years since last password change, PasswordNeverExpires and PasswordNotRequired flags, sensitive account tagging and OU path. Requires MDI.
kql:
let accountinfo = IdentityAccountInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp,*) by IdentityId
| extend DaysSinceLastPasswordChange =
    iff(isnull(LastPasswordChangeTime), int(null),
        datetime_diff('day', now(), LastPasswordChangeTime))
| extend YearsSinceLastPasswordChange =
    iff(isnull(LastPasswordChangeTime), int(null),
        datetime_diff('year', now(), LastPasswordChangeTime))   
| extend Sensitive = array_index_of(Tags, "Sensitive") != -1
| extend SensitiveLabel = iff(Sensitive == 1, "Sensitive", "Not Sensitive")
| project IdentityId, AccountUpn, AccountStatus, LastPasswordChangeTime, DaysSinceLastPasswordChange, YearsSinceLastPasswordChange, Sid, Sensitive, SensitiveLabel;
let IdInfo = IdentityInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp,*) by IdentityId
| extend PasswordNeverExpires = array_index_of(UserAccountControl, "PasswordNeverExpires") != -1,
         PasswordNotRequired = array_index_of(UserAccountControl, "PasswordNotRequired") != -1
| extend OUPath = extract(@"CN=[^,]+,(.*)", 1, DistinguishedName)
| project IdentityId, AccountName, AccountDomain, AccountDisplayName, OnPremSid, OnPremObjectId, AccountUpn, PasswordNeverExpires, PasswordNotRequired, Type, OUPath;
IdInfo
| join kind=leftouter (accountinfo) on .IdentityId == .IdentityId
| project IdentityId, AccountName, AccountStatus, AccountDomain, AccountDisplayName, AccountUpn, Sensitive, SensitiveLabel, LastPasswordChangeTime, DaysSinceLastPasswordChange, YearsSinceLastPasswordChange, PasswordNeverExpires, PasswordNotRequired, Type, OUPath
| sort by DaysSinceLastPasswordChange desc 
| where AccountStatus != "Disabled"

name: Password Age Distribution by Bucket
desc: Groups active accounts into password age buckets (0-1 years, 1-2 years, 2-5 years, 5-10 years, 10+ years). Provides a clear view of password hygiene across the organization. Essential for compliance reporting and identifying accounts with dangerously old passwords. Requires MDI.
kql:
let accountinfo = IdentityAccountInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp,*) by IdentityId
| extend DaysSinceLastPasswordChange =
    iff(isnull(LastPasswordChangeTime), int(null),
        datetime_diff('day', now(), LastPasswordChangeTime))
| project IdentityId, AccountUpn, AccountStatus, LastPasswordChangeTime, DaysSinceLastPasswordChange;
let IdInfo = IdentityInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp,*) by IdentityId
| project IdentityId, AccountName;
IdInfo
| join kind=leftouter (accountinfo) on .IdentityId == .IdentityId
| where AccountStatus != "Disabled"
| where isnotnull(LastPasswordChangeTime)
| extend PasswordAgeBucket =
    case(
        DaysSinceLastPasswordChange <= 365, "0-1 years",
        DaysSinceLastPasswordChange <= 2*365, "1-2 years",
        DaysSinceLastPasswordChange <= 5*365, "2-5 years",
        DaysSinceLastPasswordChange <= 10*365, "5-10 years",
        "10+ years")
| summarize Accounts = dcount(IdentityId) by PasswordAgeBucket
| sort by Accounts desc

name: ChatGPT Enterprise Sign-In Monitoring
desc: Monitors all sign-in activity to the ChatGPT Enterprise application (AppID: e0476654-c1d5-430b-ab80-70cbd947616a) over 180 days. Shows which users accessed ChatGPT, from where, how Conditional Access evaluated the attempt and whether MFA was required. Essential for AI governance.
kql:
let ChatGPTAppId = "e0476654-c1d5-430b-ab80-70cbd947616a";
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated >= ago(180d)
| where AppId == ChatGPTAppId
| extend
    Country = tostring(LocationDetails.countryOrRegion),
    City    = tostring(LocationDetails.city)
| project
    TimeGenerated,
    UserDisplayName,
    UserPrincipalName,
    IPAddress,
    Country,
    City,
    ConditionalAccessStatus,
    ClientAppUsed,
    AuthenticationRequirement,
    ResultType,
    ResultDescription
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: Entra ID Admin Role Assignments
desc: Lists all users with Entra ID admin role assignments from the last 30 days. Shows which accounts hold which administrative roles. Essential for privileged access reviews, least privilege enforcement and identifying over-privileged accounts.
kql:
IdentityInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where AssignedRoles != ""
| mv-expand AssignedRoles
| extend EntraAdminRole = tostring(AssignedRoles)
| project Timestamp, EntraAdminRole, AccountDisplayName
| where AccountDisplayName != ""
| sort by EntraAdminRole asc, Timestamp desc

name: Weak MFA Method Registration Detection
desc: Detects when users register or are configured with weak MFA methods: voice call (mobile/office/other), SMS (two-way/one-way). These methods are vulnerable to SIM swapping, SS7 attacks and social engineering. Any registration of weak methods should be investigated. Could indicate an attacker downgrading MFA to bypass stronger methods.
kql:
let WeakMethods = dynamic([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]);
let WeakMethodNames = dynamic(["TwoWayVoiceMobile","TwoWaySms","TwoWayVoiceOffice","TwoWayVoiceOtherMobile","TwoWaySmsOtherMobile","OneWaySms"]);
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "Update user."
| where RawEventData contains "StrongAuthenticationMethod"
| extend Target = tostring(RawEventData.ObjectId)
| extend Actor = tostring(RawEventData.UserId)
| mv-expand ModifiedProperties = parse_json(RawEventData.ModifiedProperties)
| where ModifiedProperties.Name == "StrongAuthenticationMethod"
| extend NewValue = parse_json(tostring(ModifiedProperties.NewValue))
| mv-apply NewValue on (
    extend MethodType = toint(NewValue.MethodType)
    | where MethodType in (WeakMethods)
    | summarize AddedWeakMethods = make_set(strcat(MethodType, ": ", iff(MethodType < array_length(WeakMethodNames), tostring(WeakMethodNames[MethodType]), "Unknown")))
)
| where array_length(AddedWeakMethods) > 0
| extend AddedWeakMethodsStr = tostring(AddedWeakMethods)
| project Timestamp, Actor, Target, AddedWeakMethodsStr, ReportId
| distinct *
| order by Timestamp desc

name: Sensitive Accounts List (Exposure Graph)
desc: Lists all user accounts tagged as Sensitive in Microsoft Security Exposure Management, along with their nested AD group memberships. Sensitive accounts are high-value targets. This query helps verify the sensitive account list is accurate and complete.
kql:
ExposureGraphNodes
| where NodeLabel == 'user'
| extend Tags = parse_json(tostring(parse_json(tostring(NodeProperties.rawData)).tags.[0]))
| extend NestedADGroups = parse_json(tostring(parse_json(tostring(NodeProperties.rawData)).nestedAdGroupNames))
| mv-expand NestedADGroups
| where Tags == 'Sensitive'

name: Temporary Access Pass (TAP) Usage
desc: Tracks all Temporary Access Pass creation and usage events. TAPs are time-limited credentials used for onboarding or recovery. Unauthorized TAP creation could indicate an attacker bypassing standard authentication to gain access to an account.
kql:
AuditLogs
| where Result == "success"
| where ResultDescription has "temporary access pass"
| project TimeGenerated, ResultDescription, OperationName, Identity, InitiatedBy, TargetResources
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: User URL Click Investigation
desc: Investigates all URLs clicked by specific target users that were allowed through Safe Links. Shows URL domains, click counts and timestamps. Useful for post-incident investigation when you need to know exactly what a compromised user clicked on.
kql:
// NOTE: Replace account@domain.com with the user(s) you want to investigate
let TargetUsers = dynamic(["account@domain.com"]);
UrlClickEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountUpn in~ (TargetUsers)
| where ActionType == "ClickAllowed"
| extend UrlDomain = extract("https?://([^/]+)", 1, Url)
| summarize 
    ClickedBy = make_set(AccountUpn),
    ClickedByCount = dcount(AccountUpn),
    ClickTimes = make_set(Timestamp),
    TotalClicks = count()
    by Url, UrlDomain, NetworkMessageId
| order by ClickedByCount desc, TotalClicks desc

name: Privileged Account Authentication Posture Audit
desc: Audits the authentication posture of highly privileged Entra ID accounts over 30 days using Defender XDR Advanced Hunting. Identifies privileged users across a full tiered admin role list (Tier 0/1/2) and assesses sign-in activity: total sign-ins, MFA vs single-factor sign-in counts, unique IPs and apps, and inactive privileged accounts. Each account gets a risk indicator flagging single-factor sign-ins present, no sign-ins in 30 days, or OK. Note: unlike the Sentinel SigninLogs table, EntraIdSignInEvents does not expose a per-method authentication breakdown (no FIDO2/SMS/Password granularity), so this version relies on the AuthenticationRequirement field (MFA vs single-factor) as the primary signal.
kql:
let Lookback = 30d;
let PrivilegedRoles = dynamic([
// ===== ENTRA TIER 0 (Critical - Tenant-Control) =====
	"Global Administrator",
	"Privileged Role Administrator",
	"Privileged Authentication Administrator",
	"Security Administrator",
	"Conditional Access Administrator",
	"Application Administrator",
	"Cloud Application Administrator",
	"Hybrid Identity Administrator",
	"Partner Tier2 Support",
// ===== ENTRA TIER 1 (High - Service-Control/ Writepermission) =====
	"Authentication Administrator",
	"Authentication Policy Administrator",
	"Authentication Extensibility Administrator",
	"User Administrator",
	"Helpdesk Administrator",
	"Password Administrator",
	"Directory Writers",
	"Directory Synchronization Accounts",
	"Domain Name Administrator",
	"External Identity Provider Administrator",
	"Lifecycle Workflows Administrator",
	"Groups Administrator",
	"Identity Governance Administrator",
	"Exchange Administrator",
	"SharePoint Administrator",
	"Teams Administrator",
	"Teams Telephony Administrator",
	"Skype for Business Administrator",
	"Intune Administrator",
	"Compliance Administrator",
	"Security Operator",
	"Power Platform Administrator",
	"Dynamics 365 Administrator",
	"AI Administrator",
	"Global Secure Access Administrator",
	"Attribute Assignment Administrator",
	"Attribute Provisioning Administrator",
	"B2C IEF Keyset Administrator",
	"Cloud App Security Administrator",
	"External ID User Flow Administrator",
	"Partner Tier1 Support",
	"Windows 365 Administrator",
	"Microsoft 365 Backup Administrator",
	"Microsoft 365 Migration Administrator",
	"Yammer Administrator",
	"Knowledge Administrator",
	"Billing Administrator",
// ===== ENTRA TIER 2 (Medium - Read-only / restricted) =====
	"Global Reader",
	"Security Reader",
	"Attribute Provisioning Reader",
	"Application Developer",
	"Cloud Device Administrator",
	"Azure AD Joined Device Local Administrator"
]);
let PrivilegedUsers =
	IdentityInfo
	| where Timestamp >= ago(Lookback)
	| where AssignedRoles has_any (PrivilegedRoles)
	| summarize
		AssignedRoles  = make_set(AssignedRoles),
		Department	 = take_any(Department),
		JobTitle	   = take_any(JobTitle),
		AccountEnabled = take_any(IsAccountEnabled)
		by AccountUpn;
let AuthEvents =
	EntraIdSignInEvents
	| where Timestamp >= ago(Lookback)
	| where ErrorCode == 0
	| summarize
		TotalSignins		= count(),
		LastSignin			= max(Timestamp),
		UniqueIPs			= dcount(IPAddress),
		UniqueApps			= dcount(Application),
		MFASignins			= countif(AuthenticationRequirement == "multiFactorAuthentication"),
		SingleFactorSignins	= countif(AuthenticationRequirement == "singleFactorAuthentication")
		by AccountUpn;
PrivilegedUsers
| join kind=leftouter AuthEvents
	on .AccountUpn == .AccountUpn
| project
	User				= AccountUpn,
	Roles				= AssignedRoles,
	AccountActive		= AccountEnabled,
	SigninCount			= coalesce(TotalSignins, 0),
	MFASignins			= coalesce(MFASignins, 0),
	SingleFactorSignins	= coalesce(SingleFactorSignins, 0),
	LastSignin			= LastSignin,
	UniqueIPs			= coalesce(UniqueIPs, 0),
	UniqueApps			= coalesce(UniqueApps, 0),
	RiskIndicator		= case(
		coalesce(SingleFactorSignins, 0) > 0, "Single-factor sign-ins present",
		coalesce(TotalSignins, 0) == 0,	   "No sign-ins in 30 days",
											  "OK"
	)
| where SigninCount > 0
| sort by SigninCount desc

name: New AI Agent Created With Excessive Org-Wide Sharing
desc: Detects newly created AI agents (within the last 2 days) that were configured with org-wide sharing (shared with everyone in the tenant) while also having MCP servers or declared tools attached. A brand new agent with both broad capabilities and org-wide visibility is a governance red flag, since it means anyone in the tenant can invoke an agent with tool access before it has been reviewed.
kql:
let lookback = 14d;
let recent = 2d;
let FirstSnapshot = AgentsInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where LifecycleStatus != "Deleted"
| summarize arg_min(Timestamp, *) by AgentId;
FirstSnapshot
| where CreatedDateTime > ago(recent)
| extend McpServerCount = array_length(coalesce(McpServers, dynamic([])))
| extend DeclaredToolCount = array_length(coalesce(DeclaredTools, dynamic([])))
| extend OwnerCount = array_length(coalesce(Owners, dynamic([])))
| extend IsOrgWide = set_has_element(coalesce(SharedWith, dynamic([])), "*")
| where (McpServerCount > 0 or DeclaredToolCount > 0) and IsOrgWide
| project AgentId, Name, Platform, CreatedDateTime, McpServerCount, DeclaredToolCount, OwnerCount, IsOrgWide
| sort by CreatedDateTime desc

name: Agent Configuration and Access Policy Tampering Detection
desc: Compares each AI agent current state against its 14-day baseline to detect suspicious configuration drift: instructions changed, a new MCP server added, an owner added or sharing expanded to org-wide. Flags agents where 2 or more of these signals occurred together, since a single change might be routine maintenance but multiple simultaneous changes suggest deliberate tampering to escalate an agent privileges or reach.
kql:
let lookback = 14d;
let recent = 2d;
let CurrentMcpNames = AgentsInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(recent)
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by AgentId
| where LifecycleStatus != "Deleted"
| mv-expand Mcp = McpServers
| extend McpName = tostring(Mcp.name)
| where isnotempty(McpName)
| summarize CurrentMcpServers = make_set(McpName) by AgentId;
let BaselineMcpNames = AgentsInfo
| where Timestamp between (ago(lookback) .. ago(recent))
| where LifecycleStatus != "Deleted"
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by AgentId
| mv-expand Mcp = McpServers
| extend McpName = tostring(Mcp.name)
| where isnotempty(McpName)
| summarize BaselineMcpServers = make_set(McpName) by AgentId;
let CurrentState = AgentsInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(recent)
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by AgentId
| where LifecycleStatus != "Deleted"
| project AgentId, Name, Platform, Timestamp,
    CurrentInstructions = Instructions,
    CurrentOwners = Owners,
    CurrentSharedWith = SharedWith;
let BaselineState = AgentsInfo
| where Timestamp between (ago(lookback) .. ago(recent))
| where LifecycleStatus != "Deleted"
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by AgentId
| project AgentId,
    PreviousInstructions = Instructions,
    PreviousOwners = Owners,
    BaselineSharedWith = SharedWith;
let Joined = CurrentState
| join kind=inner (BaselineState) on AgentId
| join kind=leftouter (CurrentMcpNames) on AgentId
| join kind=leftouter (BaselineMcpNames) on AgentId;
let InstructionsFlag = Joined
| where CurrentInstructions != PreviousInstructions
| project AgentId, Signal = "InstructionsChanged";
let McpFlag = Joined
| where array_length(set_difference(coalesce(CurrentMcpServers, dynamic([])), coalesce(BaselineMcpServers, dynamic([])))) > 0
| project AgentId, Signal = "NewMcpServer";
let OwnerFlag = Joined
| where array_length(set_difference(CurrentOwners, PreviousOwners)) > 0
| project AgentId, Signal = "OwnerAdded";
let SharingFlag = Joined
| where set_has_element(coalesce(CurrentSharedWith, dynamic([])), "*")
| where not(set_has_element(coalesce(BaselineSharedWith, dynamic([])), "*"))
| project AgentId, Signal = "SharingExpandedOrgWide";
union InstructionsFlag, McpFlag, OwnerFlag, SharingFlag
| summarize SignalCount = dcount(Signal), Signals = make_set(Signal) by AgentId
| where SignalCount >= 2
| join kind=inner (CurrentState) on AgentId
| project AgentId, Name, Platform, SignalCount, Signals, Timestamp
| sort by SignalCount desc

name: New Owner Role Assignment at Subscription Scope
desc: Detects when a user is granted the Owner role at subscription scope via Azure Activity Log. Owner role grants full control including the ability to assign roles to others. Subscription-scope Owner assignments outside change management are a critical privilege escalation indicator.
kql:
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationNameValue =~ 'Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write'
| where ActivityStatusValue =~ 'Succeeded'
| extend RoleAssignmentProps = parse_json(Properties)
| extend RequestBody = parse_json(tostring(RoleAssignmentProps.requestbody))
| extend RoleDefinitionId = tostring(RequestBody.Properties.RoleDefinitionId)
| where RoleDefinitionId has '8e3af657-a8ff-443c-a75c-2fe8c4bcb635' // built-in Owner role GUID
| project TimeGenerated, Caller, CallerIpAddress, ResourceId, SubscriptionId, RoleDefinitionId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: PIM Privileged Role Activation Monitoring
desc: Tracks all Privileged Identity Management (PIM) role activations from Entra ID audit logs. Shows who activated which role, when and from what IP. Establishes a baseline of normal PIM usage and helps identify off-hours activations or activations without expected justification.
kql:
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Category == 'RoleManagement'
| where ActivityDisplayName == 'Add member to role completed (PIM activation)'
| extend Actor = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| extend ActorIP = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.ipAddress)
| extend Role = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName)
| extend Hour = datetime_part('Hour', TimeGenerated)
| extend IsOffHours = Hour < 7 or Hour > 19
| project TimeGenerated, Actor, Role, ActorIP, IsOffHours, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: Direct Privileged Role Assignment Bypassing PIM
desc: Detects direct (permanent) privileged role assignments in Entra ID that bypass PIM just-in-time activation. Permanent Global Administrator or other Tier 0 role assignments outside PIM indicate either a misconfiguration or an attacker with Directory.Write permissions establishing persistent access.
kql:
// NOTE: Adjust PrivilegedRoles list to match your Tier 0 roles
let PrivilegedRoles = dynamic(['Global Administrator', 'Privileged Role Administrator', 'Security Administrator', 'Application Administrator']);
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Category == 'RoleManagement'
| where ActivityDisplayName == 'Add member to role'
| extend Role = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName)
| where Role in (PrivilegedRoles)
| extend Actor = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| extend TargetUser = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, Actor, TargetUser, Role, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: User Added to Privileged Group
desc: Detects when a user is added to a security group that grants elevated privileges (role-assignable groups or groups matching admin naming patterns). Attackers use privileged group membership as a stealthier persistence mechanism than direct role assignment since group changes are reviewed less often.
kql:
// NOTE: Adjust PrivilegedGroupNames to match your tenant's admin group naming convention
let PrivilegedGroupNames = dynamic(['Admin', 'Global Admins', 'Privileged', 'Security Admins', 'Domain Admins']);
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName == 'Add member to group'
| extend GroupName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName)
| where GroupName has_any (PrivilegedGroupNames)
| extend Actor = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| extend AddedUser = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[1].userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, Actor, AddedUser, GroupName, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: Large Blob Download from Storage Account
desc: Detects unusually large blob download volumes from Azure Storage accounts within a short window. A single caller downloading gigabytes of blob data in a short period is a strong indicator of data exfiltration, especially from storage accounts holding sensitive backups or database exports.
kql:
StorageBlobLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where OperationName == 'GetBlob'
| where StatusCode == 200
| summarize TotalBytes = sum(ResponseBodySize), RequestCount = count(), Blobs = make_set(Uri, 10)
    by CallerIpAddress, AccountName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| extend TotalMB = round(TotalBytes / 1048576.0, 1)
| where TotalMB > 500
| order by TotalMB desc

name: Bulk Storage Read Operations
desc: Detects a high volume of read operations (list, get) against a storage account from a single caller. Bulk enumeration followed by mass reads often precedes exfiltration and can also indicate a misconfigured or compromised automation identity scanning storage for sensitive files.
kql:
StorageBlobLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where OperationName in ('GetBlob', 'ListBlobs', 'GetBlobProperties')
| summarize ReadOps = count(), UniqueBlobs = dcount(Uri) by CallerIpAddress, AccountName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where ReadOps > 500
| order by ReadOps desc

name: Guest User Invited to Tenant
desc: Tracks all guest user invitations sent to external identities. Shows who invited whom, from which domain and whether the invite was accepted. Establishes a baseline of expected B2B collaboration and helps catch invitations to unexpected or personal email domains.
kql:
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName == 'Invite external user'
| extend InvitedBy = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| extend InvitedEmail = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].userPrincipalName)
| extend InvitedDomain = tolower(tostring(split(InvitedEmail, '@')[-1]))
| project TimeGenerated, InvitedBy, InvitedEmail, InvitedDomain, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: App Registration Redirect URI Modified
desc: Detects when the redirect URI of an app registration is modified. Attackers who compromise an application owner account can add a redirect URI pointing to attacker-controlled infrastructure, silently redirecting OAuth authorization codes and tokens to themselves.
kql:
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName == 'Update application'
| extend ModifiedProps = parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].modifiedProperties
| mv-expand ModifiedProps
| where tostring(ModifiedProps.displayName) has 'RedirectUri'
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName)
| extend ModifiedBy = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| extend OldValue = tostring(ModifiedProps.oldValue)
| extend NewValue = tostring(ModifiedProps.newValue)
| project TimeGenerated, AppName, ModifiedBy, OldValue, NewValue
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: Federated Identity Credential Added
desc: Detects when a Federated Identity Credential (FIC) is added to an app registration or service principal. FIC abuse is a modern, high-impact persistence technique: attackers add a federated trust to an external identity provider (like GitHub Actions) they control, allowing token issuance without ever touching a client secret.
kql:
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has_any ('Add federated identity credential', 'Update application - Certificates and secrets management')
| where tostring(TargetResources) has 'federatedIdentityCredentials'
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName)
| extend ModifiedBy = coalesce(tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName), tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).app.displayName))
| project TimeGenerated, AppName, ModifiedBy, OperationName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: Diagnostic Settings Deleted
desc: Detects deletion of diagnostic settings on Azure resources. Diagnostic settings control what telemetry flows to Log Analytics and Sentinel. Deleting them is a defense evasion technique that blinds detection for the affected resource before further malicious activity.
kql:
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationNameValue =~ 'microsoft.insights/diagnosticSettings/delete'
| where ActivityStatusValue =~ 'Succeeded'
| project TimeGenerated, Caller, CallerIpAddress, ResourceId, SubscriptionId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: Azure Policy Deleted or Disabled
desc: Detects deletion or disabling of Azure Policy assignments. Azure Policy often enforces security baselines (deny public IPs, require encryption, restrict regions). Removing a policy assignment can be a precursor to deploying non-compliant, insecure resources undetected.
kql:
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationNameValue in ('Microsoft.Authorization/policyAssignments/delete', 'Microsoft.Authorization/policyAssignments/write')
| where ActivityStatusValue =~ 'Succeeded'
| project TimeGenerated, OperationNameValue, Caller, CallerIpAddress, ResourceId, SubscriptionId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: Conditional Access Policy Modified or Deleted
desc: Detects creation, modification or deletion of Conditional Access policies. CA policies enforce MFA, block legacy auth and restrict risky sign-ins. Unauthorized changes here are one of the highest-impact defense evasion techniques in Entra ID, potentially disabling MFA enforcement tenant-wide.
kql:
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has_any ('Add conditional access policy', 'Update conditional access policy', 'Delete conditional access policy')
| extend PolicyName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName)
| extend ModifiedBy = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, PolicyName, ModifiedBy, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: Defender for Cloud Alert Suppression Created
desc: Detects creation of Microsoft Defender for Cloud alert suppression rules. Suppression rules silently dismiss future alerts matching specific criteria. An attacker with sufficient access can create a broad suppression rule to hide their own future activity from the security team.
kql:
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationNameValue has 'Microsoft.Security/alertsSuppressionRules'
| where ActivityStatusValue =~ 'Succeeded'
| project TimeGenerated, OperationNameValue, Caller, CallerIpAddress, ResourceId, SubscriptionId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: NSG Open Inbound Rule Added
desc: Detects new Network Security Group rules that allow inbound traffic from any source (0.0.0.0/0 or Internet tag) on any port or sensitive management ports (22, 3389, 445). This is a classic technique to expose a resource to the internet for later exploitation.
kql:
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationNameValue =~ 'Microsoft.Network/networkSecurityGroups/securityRules/write'
| where ActivityStatusValue =~ 'Succeeded'
| extend RuleProps = parse_json(tostring(parse_json(Properties).requestbody))
| extend SourceAddressPrefix = tostring(RuleProps.properties.sourceAddressPrefix)
| extend DestPortRange = tostring(RuleProps.properties.destinationPortRange)
| extend Direction = tostring(RuleProps.properties.direction)
| extend Access = tostring(RuleProps.properties.access)
| where Direction == 'Inbound' and Access == 'Allow'
| where SourceAddressPrefix in ('*', '0.0.0.0/0', 'Internet')
| project TimeGenerated, Caller, CallerIpAddress, ResourceId, DestPortRange, SourceAddressPrefix
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: Key Vault Secret and Key Enumeration
desc: Detects high-volume list/enumeration operations against Azure Key Vault (SecretList, KeyList, CertificateList). Mass enumeration of vault contents from a single identity is a reconnaissance step commonly seen before targeted secret retrieval in a credential access attack chain.
kql:
AzureDiagnostics
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ResourceProvider == 'MICROSOFT.KEYVAULT'
| where OperationName in ('SecretList', 'KeyList', 'CertificateList')
| summarize ListOps = count() by CallerIPAddress, identity_claim_upn_s, Resource, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where ListOps > 20
| order by ListOps desc

name: First-Time Key Vault Secret Access
desc: Compares current-day Key Vault secret GET operations against a 30-day baseline of caller-to-vault access patterns. A caller retrieving a secret from a vault they have never accessed before is a strong signal of either lateral movement or a compromised identity exploring new resources.
kql:
let Baseline = AzureDiagnostics
| where TimeGenerated between (ago(30d) .. ago(1d))
| where ResourceProvider == 'MICROSOFT.KEYVAULT'
| where OperationName == 'SecretGet'
| distinct identity_claim_upn_s, Resource;
AzureDiagnostics
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ResourceProvider == 'MICROSOFT.KEYVAULT'
| where OperationName == 'SecretGet'
| where isnotempty(identity_claim_upn_s)
| join kind=leftanti (Baseline) on identity_claim_upn_s, Resource
| project TimeGenerated, identity_claim_upn_s, Resource, CallerIPAddress, requestUri_s
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: VM Extension Silently Installed
desc: Detects installation of VM extensions, especially CustomScriptExtension and RunCommand which allow arbitrary code execution on a virtual machine. Attackers with Contributor access to a VM (without needing OS-level credentials) can use extensions to run commands, install backdoors or exfiltrate data.
kql:
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationNameValue =~ 'Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/extensions/write'
| where ActivityStatusValue =~ 'Succeeded'
| extend ExtensionProps = parse_json(tostring(parse_json(Properties).requestbody))
| extend ExtensionType = tostring(ExtensionProps.properties.type)
| where ExtensionType has_any ('CustomScript', 'RunCommand', 'DSC')
| project TimeGenerated, Caller, CallerIpAddress, ResourceId, ExtensionType
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: Automation Runbook Created or Modified
desc: Detects creation or modification of Azure Automation runbooks. Automation accounts often hold powerful managed identities with subscription-wide permissions. A newly created or modified runbook can be used as a persistence and execution mechanism that runs on a schedule under a privileged identity.
kql:
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationNameValue has_any ('Microsoft.Automation/automationAccounts/runbooks/write', 'Microsoft.Automation/automationAccounts/runbooks/draft/write')
| where ActivityStatusValue =~ 'Succeeded'
| project TimeGenerated, Caller, CallerIpAddress, ResourceId, SubscriptionId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: Mass Azure Resource Deletion
desc: Detects a high volume of resource delete operations from a single caller within a short time window. Mass deletion of resources is a classic impact technique used in the final stage of an attack, often to destroy evidence or cause maximum business disruption before detection.
kql:
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where OperationNameValue endswith '/delete'
| where ActivityStatusValue =~ 'Succeeded'
| summarize DeleteCount = count(), Resources = make_set(ResourceId, 20) by Caller, CallerIpAddress, bin(TimeGenerated, 30m)
| where DeleteCount > 15
| order by DeleteCount desc

name: Subscription Ownership Transfer
desc: Detects Azure subscription ownership transfer requests and acceptances. Transferring subscription ownership hands full control (including billing) to a different account or tenant. Any unexpected transfer request is a critical event requiring immediate verification, as it can be used to hijack an entire subscription.
kql:
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationNameValue has_any ('Microsoft.Subscription/transfer', 'Microsoft.Subscription/acceptOwnership', 'transferSubscription')
| project TimeGenerated, OperationNameValue, Caller, CallerIpAddress, ActivityStatusValue, SubscriptionId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

name: Sign-In After Long Dormancy
desc: Detects successful sign-ins from accounts with no sign-in activity in the preceding 60 days. Dormant account reactivation is a common pattern in account takeover: attackers target stale accounts that owners rarely check, reducing the chance of the compromise being noticed quickly.
kql:
let Lookback = 90d;
let DormancyThresholdDays = 60;
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where ResultType == '0'
| order by UserPrincipalName, TimeGenerated asc
| serialize
| extend PrevSignIn = prev(TimeGenerated), PrevUser = prev(UserPrincipalName)
| where UserPrincipalName == PrevUser
| extend GapDays = datetime_diff('day', TimeGenerated, PrevSignIn)
| where GapDays >= DormancyThresholdDays
| project UserPrincipalName, PreviousSignIn = PrevSignIn, ReactivationSignIn = TimeGenerated, GapDays, IPAddress
| order by GapDays desc

name: Credential-Named Files in SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams
desc: Cloud half of the credential file sweep. Finds files with credential-like names across SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams file operations. Groups by file rather than event so you get a remediation list, not an event log. DistinctUsers is the column that matters: nine people opening the same Service Accounts.xlsx is a finding.
kql:
let Lookback = 30d;
let CredentialTerms = @"(?i)(password|passwrd|passwd|pwd|passcode|credential|creds|logins|secret|apikey|api[_\- ]key|privatekey|id_rsa)";
let BenignTerms = @"(?i)(compass|passport|passenger|passive|passage|bypass|encompass|surpass|secretar|secret santa|passwordless|password[_\- ]?polic|password[_\- ]?manager|password[_\- ]?expir|(reset|change|forgot)[_\- ]?password|password[_\- ]?(reset|change)|credential[_\- ]?guard)";
let DocExtensions = dynamic(["txt","csv","xls","xlsx","xlsm","doc","docx","rtf","one","md","json","yaml","yml","xml","ini","cfg","conf","env","ps1","bat","sql","pdf","pem","ppk","key","rdp","bak"]);
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where RecordType == "SharePointFileOperation"
| where UserId !~ "app@sharepoint"
| where isnotempty(SourceFileName)
| where SourceFileName matches regex CredentialTerms
| where not(SourceFileName matches regex BenignTerms)
| where SourceFileExtension in~ (DocExtensions)
| extend Estate = iff(Site_Url has "/personal/", "OneDrive", "SharePoint")
| extend TeamsChatFile = SourceRelativeUrl has "Microsoft Teams Chat Files"
| extend OwnerPath = extract(@"/personal/([^/]+)", 1, tolower(Site_Url))
| summarize
    FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
    Touches = count(),
    DistinctUsers = dcount(UserId),
    TouchedBy = make_set(UserId, 25),
    Operations = make_set(Operation, 10),
    ClientIPs = make_set(ClientIP, 10)
  by SourceFileName, SourceFileExtension, Estate, TeamsChatFile, OwnerPath, Site_Url, SourceRelativeUrl
| extend FullPath = strcat(Site_Url, SourceRelativeUrl, "/", SourceFileName)
| project FirstSeen, LastSeen, SourceFileName, SourceFileExtension, Estate, TeamsChatFile,
          OwnerPath, DistinctUsers, TouchedBy, Touches, Operations, ClientIPs, FullPath
| sort by DistinctUsers desc, LastSeen desc

name: Credential Discovery on Endpoints (T1552.001)
desc: Somebody shopping for the loot. Detects endpoint processes running credential search commands (findstr, Select-String, grep, reg query, recursive gci) targeting password credential and secret terms. Standard post-compromise recon under T1552.001 Unsecured Credentials in Files. Fast quiet and one of the first things an attacker runs after landing.
kql:
let Lookback = 30d;
let SearchTools = dynamic(["findstr", "Select-String", "sls", "grep", "reg", "Get-ChildItem", "gci"]);
let CredentialTargets = @"(?i)(password|passwd|pwd|passcode|credential|creds|secret|unattend|sysprep)";
let RecursiveFlags = @"(?i)(-recurse|/s\b|/si\b|\s-r\b|\*\.|--include)";
DeviceProcessEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where isnotempty(ProcessCommandLine)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (SearchTools)
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex CredentialTargets
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex RecursiveFlags
| extend Actor = tolower(iff(isnotempty(AccountUpn), AccountUpn, strcat(AccountDomain, @"\", AccountName)))
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, Actor, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          Parent = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          Grandparent = InitiatingProcessParentFileName, ReportId
| sort by TimeGenerated desc
